title: Behavior toggles and back-compat test harness for API evolution
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Add a runtime behaviour-toggle system and a reproducible compatibility test harness to support phased deprecations for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. Provide an SDK migration helper and CI gating to prevent accidental regressions when behavior flags are flipped.
background: We are rolling out a set of API changes that tighten structured-output validation, change streaming chunk boundaries, and modify the default tool-call resolution order. Historically we've used ad-hoc flags and manual smoke tests; that approach has led to regressions in two customer incidents (See ENG-6580). PM has requested a formal, repeatable path for turning off legacy behaviors with clear telemetry and SDK assist to reduce migration friction.
goals: Provide a runtime toggle layer that can safely route requests to legacy or new behavior by header or tenant config
Ship a reproducible test harness (compat-runner) that runs canonical prompt sets across old/new code paths and reports a compatibility score
Add SDK helpers (node/py/go) to surface compatibility warnings and automated migrations for common patterns
Enforce compatibility checks in main CI to block behavior-flag flips that reduce the compatibility score below threshold
scope: Runtime toggle implementation (server-side) and admin UI to flip per-tenant flags
Compat-runner harness and golden prompt corpus for streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs
CI integration and a daily compat-report dashboard
SDK deprecation helpers and opt-in migration tooling
Monitoring and alerting for customer-facing regressions during rollout
proposed_approach: Introduce X-RW-Compat header that accepts a comma-separated list of named toggles (e.g., streaming-v2, toolcall-order-v1, strict-json-output)
Persist tenant toggle preferences in the control plane; default to legacy for 90 days then auto-escalate unless opt-out is set
Build compat-runner as a lightweight test container that plays golden prompts against both code paths, diffs token-level outputs and structured parse trees, and computes a compatibility score
Define compatibility score thresholds per-feature (e.g., streaming: 0.95, tool-calls: 0.98) and tie to CI gates
Expose SDK warnings when client detects server-side toggles that could affect request semantics and offer inline code fixes or examples
Backfill telemetry for divergence classes (truncation, extra tokens, semantic drift, tool-binding mismatches) and surface in Console as a per-tenant report
test_plan: Create golden corpus: 1k prompts covering streaming edge cases, tool-call selection heuristics, and structured JSON outputs
Implement compat-runner to run corpus nightly against prod-staging and compare to prod-stable
Add unit tests that assert deterministic KV cache behavior when toggles are enabled/disabled
Integrate compat-runner into PR workflow: PRs that modify behavior code must include compat-runner results
Run canary rollout on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks and monitor compatibility dashboard and alert if score drops >2% for two consecutive days
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts X-RW-Compat header and honors per-tenant toggles
Compat-runner implemented, runs in CI, and produces a per-feature compatibility score report
SDKs (python/node) include runtime-toggle introspection and at least one automated migration snippet
Regression dashboard shows historical baseline and can alert on deviations
Canary rollout completed for one toggle (streaming-v2) with no customer-facing incidents for 14 days
